summary: [OBS] The direct first-+30-touch evidence is a mixture: 582 A_pm touchers over 470 days, 351 (60.3%) later trade at least +10% above the touch-bar close and 231 (39.7%) do not. The new time split is economically suggestive but not a validated policy: <10:00 n=242 has touch-close→EOD mean -9.29% (continuation share .649), while 10:00–11:00 n=167 is +1.11% (.581), 11:00–13:00 n=83 is +6.35% (.590), and 13:00+ n=90 is +2.60% (.533). Halt strata are non-monotone in continuation probability and mostly have negative medians despite positive means at 4–5 and 6+ halts. [INFERENCE] The fade is conditional in raw mark space, but the late positive mean is likely a right-tail lottery: the independent afternoon artifact has pooled mean +1.29%, median -3.57%, positive share 38.8%, and the top five observations contribute 202% of the sum (mean excluding top five about -1.3%). [OBS] The only executable policy actually run is unconditional all-+30 exit at the next bar open; it beats hold-to-close in both blocks (N=2/100 bps +0.894%/day pooled, +0.344% block1, +2.110% block2). Therefore a conditional hold has not been shown to beat unconditional selling; it is a plausible mechanism hypothesis requiring one event-level, next-open, day-clustered policy comparison.

architecture: The evidence is layered rather than event-linked. touch_mixture/touch_halt_time_splits/continuation_identifiability/afternoon_touch_continuation are descriptive path scans over first-touch observations. F2_F12/surface.json and capital_allocation_map/relationship_tables.json are fixed-checkpoint state-to-future-outcome maps. T5_paths is trade-level path chronology, while F8/joint_surface is unconditional basket accounting. HARVEST is the only tested executable first-+30 release family; it uses completed-bar detection and next-bar-open execution. None of the persisted artifacts currently joins a first-touch row to an executable conditional hold-versus-sell P&L, and the newest split JSONs have no committed producer/provenance script.
report:
## Direct continuation table (what is actually persisted)

Source for the first three rows: `factory/artifacts/basket/phase2/DIAGNOSTICS_20260924/touch_mixture.json` and `touch_fade_paths.json`. The binary continuation label is post-touch maximum >= +10% relative to the touch-bar close.

| post-touch outcome | n | share | continuation share | post-touch max mean | touch-bar close -> EOD mean | median / positive share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| All first +30% touchers | 582 | 100.0% | 60.31% | not persisted | -2.23% | -10.8% / 30.6% |
| Fade: post-touch max < +10% | 231 | 39.7% | 0% | +4.00% | -19.66% | about -19.4% (reported in `researches/SWARM-SYNTHESIS-20260924.md`) |
| Continue: post-touch max >= +10% | 351 | 60.3% | 100% | +52.34% | +9.23% | about -3.3% (reported in the synthesis) |
| First +50% touch (nested, not an eventual-outcome bin) | 297 | — | not persisted | not persisted | -1.79% | -12.4% / 29.6% |
| First +100% touch (nested, not an eventual-outcome bin) | 105 | — | not persisted | not persisted | +0.85% | -13.6% / 36.2% |

[OBS] The +100% first-touch cohort has a slightly positive mean touch-close-to-EOD mark, unlike +30% and +50%, but its median is still -13.6% and only 36.2% finish positive. [INFERENCE] Extreme first-touch cohorts contain some large survivors, but “extreme excursion” is not equivalent to a positive close-to-close hold. The +50% and +100% rows are nested threshold cohorts, not the requested post-touch eventual-outcome bins.

### Requested three-way eventual-outcome split

The requested labels `fade <= +10%`, `+30..+100%`, and `+100%+` are not persisted as counts or continuation statistics. The only exact eventual split available is the binary 231/351 split above. Relabeling the first +50/+100 touch rows as eventual outcomes would be a semantic error. This is the first missing deliverable.

## Time-of-first-touch table

Source: `factory/artifacts/basket/phase2/DIAGNOSTICS_20260924/touch_halt_time_splits.json`, key `by_touch_time`; medians are reported in `researches/SWARM-SYNTHESIS-20260924.md`, section 1.4, but are not fields in the JSON itself.

| first +30% touch time | n | share | continuation share | touch close -> EOD mean | median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| before 10:00 | 242 | 41.6% | 64.88% | -9.29% | -18.3% |
| 10:00–11:00 | 167 | 28.7% | 58.08% | +1.11% | -12.9% |
| 11:00–13:00 | 83 | 14.3% | 59.04% | +6.35% | -4.7% |
| 13:00+ | 90 | 15.5% | 53.33% | +2.60% | -0.7% |

[OBS] The early-touch majority is strongly negative; all three later bins have positive means, especially 11:00–13:00. [OBS] The continuation probability is not monotone in the same way: it is highest before 10:00 and lowest after 13:00. [INFERENCE] Early continuers apparently tend to produce smaller gains and/or the early faders lose more, while later touchers contain fewer but much larger survivors. Therefore the decision target should be expected executable `hold minus sell` return, not the binary probability of trading another +10%.

[INFERENCE] A simple touch-close reference calculation gives late-touch (>=10:00) n=340 and a weighted mean mark of about +2.78% across the 10–11, 11–13, and 13+ bins. If early names were sold at the touch close and late names held, the descriptive mark advantage would be about +1.63 percentage points per all toucher before next-open gap, friction, cash, and exposure-time effects. This is an upper-bound intuition, not a policy result: the action cannot execute at the touch-bar close, and the late mean is not shown to be robust.

## Pre-touch halt-count table

Source: `touch_halt_time_splits.json`, key `by_halts`; medians again come from the synthesis report rather than the JSON.

| halts before touch | n | share | continuation share | touch close -> EOD mean | median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0–1 | 416 | 71.5% | 62.50% | -2.14% | -11.0% |
| 2–3 | 73 | 12.5% | 54.79% | -10.69% | -14.5% |
| 4–5 | 29 | 5.0% | 58.62% | +0.43% | -13.8% |
| 6+ | 64 | 11.0% | 53.13% | +5.61% | -5.9% |

[OBS] Halt count is not a clean continuation classifier: 6+ halts has the highest positive mean but the lowest continuation share, and every reported median remains negative. [INFERENCE] High halt intensity may be a proxy for extreme volatility and occasional very large survivors, not a safe “hold” state. The 4–5 and 6+ cells total only 93 observations, so a compound time×halt rule would be especially vulnerable to noise and confounding.

[OBS] `factory/scripts/basket_anatomy.py::ngaps` counts any inter-bar gap > 1 minute, while the project’s halt diagnostics use >=5-minute holes (for example `runner_phenom.py` and `halt_temporal.py`). `factory/artifacts/basket/sip/README.md` explicitly says no LULD status is exposed and halts are inferred from event-stream gaps. A direct halt-conditioned policy must use one predeclared definition (preferably >=5-minute holes) and report sparse-name exclusions; it cannot reuse `gap_pre/gap_post` as if they were halt counts.

## Independent check of the late-positive thesis

Source: `factory/artifacts/basket/phase2/DIAGNOSTICS_20260924/afternoon_touch_continuation.json`.

[OBS] For first +30% touches at/after 11:00, pooled across A_pm, A_open, and B600: n=562 over 364 days, mean +1.29%, median -3.57%, positive share 38.8%; family means are A_pm +4.40% (n=173), A_open +3.45% (n=160), and B600 -2.58% (n=229). [OBS] The top five observations account for 202.42% of the sum; the reported mean excluding them is about -1.3%. [INFERENCE] The late positive mean is a lottery-shaped cross-family result, not demonstrated drift. The A_pm late subset is the relevant one for this assignment, but its family-specific top-five concentration is not persisted, so the steelman remains unproven.

This is the key disagreement with a strong “late touch = continuation” reading: the time split is a useful anatomical contrast, but it does not by itself establish an executable afternoon hold.

## Rank and giveback: direct touch evidence versus checkpoint proxies

### Direct touch-moment comparison

Source: `continuation_identifiability.json`, n=582.

| feature at touch | continuers mean | faders mean |
|---|---:|---:|
| rank | 2.063 | 1.922 |
| drawdown from running high | -2.72% | -3.09% |
| halts so far | 2.895 | 5.048 |
| minutes since fill | 80.83 | 99.16 |
| entry-to-touch return | +31.00% | +30.18% |
| five-bar velocity | +16.28% | +13.50% |
| touch-bar/session volume ratio | 3.10 | 3.67 |

[OBS] The entry-to-touch move is essentially identical across continuers and faders, directly contradicting a simple “small excursion fades, large excursion continues” story. Rank level and giveback are close as well. [OBS] The synthesis reports weak AUCs (roughly .43–.57), but those AUC values are not persisted in `continuation_identifiability.json`; they should be treated as report-only until the producer is recovered.

### Fixed-checkpoint proxy evidence

`F2_F12/surface.json` and `capital_allocation_map/relationship_tables.json` are not first-touch tables: they use fixed ET checkpoints and outcomes strictly after the checkpoint. They nevertheless show why rank trajectory, giveback, and MFE-so-far deserve a direct event study.

[OBS] At A_pm ET600 in `capital_allocation_map/relationship_tables.json`, rank_change <=0 (stable/improved) versus >0 (worsened) has all-row remaining-MFE mean 18.37% versus 10.37% in block1 and 24.09% versus 14.73% in block2; future +50 touch probability is 8.94% versus 2.87% and 11.48% versus 5.92%. [INFERENCE] Rank *trajectory* is a more credible conditional coordinate than the nearly identical final rank level in the direct touch artifact.

[OBS] At the same checkpoint, the deepest drawdown-from-running-high bucket has all-row remaining MFE 15.17% versus 7.00% in block1 and 20.07% versus 10.93% in block2; future +50 probability is 4.82% versus 1.68% and 10.08% versus 3.10%. But the deepest bucket has 100% adverse-first under the panel definition versus 8.4%/12.2% in the shallowest bucket. [INFERENCE] Giveback can mark a convex rebound opportunity while simultaneously marking a much worse failure regime; it is not a standalone hold signal.

[OBS] MFE-so-far at ET600 is similarly graded: the highest bucket has all-row remaining MFE 20.69% versus 7.10% in the lowest bucket (block1), and 21.49% versus 8.48% (block2); future +50 is 9.01% versus 1.81% and 10.66% versus 2.65%. [INFERENCE] “Already extreme” can predict more future tail, but the associated adverse tail and sample clustering must be priced. These are checkpoint proxies, not evidence that a first +30 toucher with the same state will hold profitably.

## What the prior code actually tested

1. `factory/scripts/basket_diag_harvest.py::HarvestAt` checks `bar["high"]` on a completed bar, sets a done flag, and schedules a 100% `EXIT`; `basket_sim.py::simulate_day` executes pending actions at the first later bar open. The `HARVEST` design string explicitly says next-bar-open execution. The tested arms are hold, 50% cuts at +30/+50/+100, and 100% all30. No first-touch-time-conditioned hold arm exists.
2. `factory/scripts/basket_f2_f12.py::checkpoint_row` uses state through fixed checkpoints (`et <= tp`) and targets bars strictly after `tp`. It does not create a first-touch event row and computes no action P&L. `F2_F12/README.md` says outcomes are descriptive, not executable.
3. `factory/scripts/basket_anatomy.py::ladders/attach_path` records first ladder touches, fill, peak, MAE, EOD, and `gap_pre/gap_post`; it has no true halt-count field and no post-touch continuation outcome.
4. `factory/scripts/basket_t5_rawpaths.py::path_stats` is a genuine trade-level chronology with actual fill as state zero and MFE strata; it has no rank/halt and no first-touch conditional policy.
5. `factory/scripts/basket_f8_joint.py` summarizes already-run unconditional basket cells. `F8/README.md` explicitly says F1 tickets have no rank field and that golden-window conditional results are not in F8.
6. `factory/scripts/basket_diag_segment.py` tests exits at fixed ET580/600/630, not first-touch time. Its +145 bps/day ET600 improvement is a clock-exit result, not evidence for holding late +30 touchers.
7. `factory/scripts/basket_diag_derisk.py` tests fixed ET600 state cuts. It is not a time-of-touch or peak-relative-at-touch policy.

## Bugs / semantic mismatches that change the interpretation

- **Touch mark versus executable exit:** `touch_fade_paths.json` defines touch-to-EOD from the touch-bar close. `exit_convention_comparison.json` shows for +30 that next-open-to-EOD is -2.35% versus touch-close-to-EOD -2.23%; for +50 it is -2.11% versus -1.79%. The path scan is anatomical, not a fill model.
- **No event-level intersection:** F2/capital-map state surfaces and touch scans use different populations and timing. Their apparent agreement is hypothesis-generating only.
- **Nested cohorts:** first +30, first +50, and first +100 rows are nested; they cannot be treated as independent outcome bins.
- **Provenance gap:** the new `touch_halt_time_splits.json`, `touch_mixture.json`, `continuation_identifiability.json`, and `afternoon_touch_continuation.json` have no corresponding committed producer under `factory/scripts/`, unlike T5/F2/F8/HARVEST. The synthesis contains medians/AUCs not present in the JSONs. Preserve this caveat.
- **Execution censoring:** the pre-registration requires a final-bar touch to be non-executable/N/A, not replaced by its close. The current split summaries do not report final-bar touch counts.
- **Family mixing:** `afternoon_touch_continuation.json` pools A_pm, A_open, and B600; its B600 mean is negative while A_pm/A_open are positive. It cannot be used as a universal late-touch rule.
- **Day clustering:** 582 tickets occur on 470 days; ticket-level standard errors would understate uncertainty. Any policy comparison must aggregate/bootstrap by day.

## Explicit answer: does a conditional hold beat unconditional selling?

**Not established.** [OBS] The only tested causal policy is all30 next-open exit, and it beats hold-to-close in both blocks: N=2/100 bps `delta_vs_hold=+0.00894` pooled, `+0.00344` block1, `+0.02110` block2; N=3/100 bps is `+0.00661` pooled, `+0.00330` block1, `+0.01392` block2. [OBS] The average deployed capital falls under all30, so the apparent gain is substantially exposure-time reduction, not proof that the touch is a superior exit price. [INFERENCE] A late-touch hold has a plausible raw-mark upside, but the current evidence does not show that its executable next-open return, net of friction and exposure, beats the already-measured all-sell control. The honest current decision is therefore “conditional hold remains an untested hypothesis,” not “conditional hold wins” or “the right tail is universally a hold phenomenon.”

## Smallest study that would settle it

Run one bounded event-level pass over the existing 582 A_pm first-+30 touchers; do not run a parameter grid.

For each `(date,ticker)` record:

- first-touch ET, touch-bar close, next-bar open, and `exec_present`;
- running high through the touch bar and `giveback = 1 - touch_close / running_high`;
- halt count before the touch using a single >=5-minute-gap definition;
- rank at the last causal snapshot at/before touch, rank change, minutes since fill, and time-of-touch bin;
- post-touch max, post-touch MAE, final close, and block1/block2 labels;
- exact eventual bins relative to touch-bar close: `F: <=+10%`, `M: +30..+100%`, `E: >=+100%` (retain the omitted +10..+30 mass rather than silently folding it).

Report per stratum: n tickets, n distinct days, mean/median/positive share for touch-close→EOD and next-open→EOD, post-touch max/MAE, block split, and day-clustered uncertainty. Add a 2D time×halt table and time×giveback/rank-change table before considering a compound rule.

Then run exactly one predeclared policy comparison in the existing engine: all30 control versus `EXIT at first +30 only when first-touch ET < 600; otherwise HOLD`, at N=2/3 and 100/150 bps, with next-open execution, forced-flat/cash/carry semantics unchanged. Do not tune 10:00/11:00/13:00 or halt cutoffs. A high-halt condition should wait for the 2D table; do not combine time and halt post hoc.

A meaningful result would be positive incremental C0 EV of the conditional policy over all-sell in both development blocks after realistic friction, with positive per-deployed-dollar economics and a result that is not solely one or two giant observations. A negative median is not automatically disqualifying for a genuine convex payoff, but a positive mean that disappears under the top-five check, block split, or day-clustered policy simulation should be labeled a lottery, not a hold edge. If the late policy fails, the evidence supports retaining unconditional selling as the measured implementation while leaving the convexity mechanism open for finer state or execution data.
